summary: Boiler-plate bottle light of 1903 at Buffalo's new breakwater; moved in 1985 to the Coast Guard grounds beside Buffalo Main Light.

structures.note: Bottle-shaped boiler-plate tower, 3/8 inch plate, base 10 ft 3/4 in; total height 23 ft 3/4 in with the ventilator ball (LighthouseFriends). Moved from the breakwater in 1985.

access.note: Grounds open on the Coast Guard station beside Buffalo Main Lighthouse; tower closed to visitors (LighthouseFriends). Public access was restored in late 2011.

events.note: Act of 6 June 1900 appropriated $45,000 for light and fog-signal stations at the main southern entrance of the new breakwater
Plans for the towers and fog-signal house changed after two severe storms; the report does not date the storms. Modified plans practically complete by 30 June 1901
Temporary red post lantern set on the southern end of the breakwater until the permanent light was ready
Permanent bottle light installed on the breakwater
Permanent light first shown on the breakwater
Barbier, Benard & Turenne lens lantern giving a fixed red light, maintained by the keeper of Buffalo Main Lighthouse
Battery-operated 12-volt lamp installed atop the tower; ventilator ball removed
Listed on the National Register as Buffalo North Breakwater South End Light (NRIS 83001669)
Light served on the breakwater until 1985
Removed from the breakwater to a new home beside the original 1833 Buffalo Main Lighthouse
Public access restored in late 2011 after the Coast Guard gave up land around the light under a 2010 deal

corrections.proposed: Buffalo North Breakwater South End Light
corrections.why: The register number on this record (NRIS 83001669) is titled Buffalo North Breakwater South End Light on the National Park Service listing. LighthouseFriends calls the same light North Breakwater South Side. East End appears to be a name from another source that the register does not use. Human check: East End may be kept as an other name.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's coordinates are the light's present position beside Buffalo Main Lighthouse, as LighthouseFriends gives them. The record notes that two sources place the structure more than 500 m apart; the breakwater site it was moved from is not given in any source I could cite, so the conflict is not resolved here.
Three names are in use: the register and the 1979 survey title (South End), LighthouseFriends (South Side), and the record's East End. The story uses the register name.

notes_for_editor: IDENTITY. The record names this light East End; the register (NRIS 83001669) and LighthouseFriends' citation of the 1979 HAER survey use South End; LighthouseFriends' own title is North Breakwater South Side. Wikipedia has separate articles for the East End and South End lights that describe the same bottle light; Wikipedia is used for leads only, so none of its figures are cited. HEIGHT. The record gives 8.8 m (29 ft). LighthouseFriends gives 23 ft 3/4 in total with the ventilator ball (about 7.0 m); the story and the structure entry use LighthouseFriends. No citable source for 8.8 m was read. STRUCTURES. The record lists two towers built 1903; only one bottle light is supported here. The second entry is unexplained and may be a duplicate. The South Buffalo North Side light (us-ny-south-buffalo-north-side, NRIS 83001673) is a separate 1903 light with its own register number. POSITION. The record's coordinates are the present site. The sources read give no citable original breakwater position. KEEPERS. No keeper is named for this light. The USLHS roster for Buffalo Breakwater North End (25 lines, 1872-1914) belongs to the older station (us-ny-buffalo-breakwater-north-end, lost, with a 1914 rebuild) and is not used here. ENTRANCE NAME. The 1900 and 1901 Board entries say southern entrance; LighthouseFriends says it marked the northern entrance. The story reports both without choosing. Board volume labels are cited by fiscal year ended 30 June. The 1901 entry was located on scan page 217 with corpus.py page (lhb 1901 'southern entrance') and is cited by that page. The NRHP nomination is not digitised (22 KB placeholder). Newspaper search (Chronicling America, 'north breakwater' with 'light', New York papers, 1902 to 1904) returned no hits; nothing from newspapers is used.
